last_digest.title: North Korean hackers behind major open-source supply chain attacks, Amazon says
last_digest.rss_summary: A North Korea-linked hacker group was behind several high-profile compromises of open-source software libraries used by developers worldwide, researchers have found.

Web applications have never been more exposed or more critical to secure. Huntress analyzes a real-world intrusion to show how threat actors establish persistence, disable defenses, and reshape compromised systems, and why defenders must investigate the original entry point rather than simply remove the malware. last_digest.title: CareCloud Data Breach Impacts Over 350,000
last_digest.rss_summary:
In March 2026, hackers stole personal, financial, and medical information from the company’s AWS environment.
The post CareCloud Data Breach Impacts Over 350,000 appeared first on SecurityWeek.

last_week_digest.title: Swiss rail manufacturer Stadler refuses to pay $12.3 million ransom after cyberattack
last_week_digest.tldr: Swiss rail manufacturer Stadler has rejected a 12.3 million dollar ransom demand from the Everest gang following a supplier data breach. While operations remain unaffected, the incident signals that the digitising rail sector is becoming a primary target for sophisticated, extortion-focused cybercriminal syndicates globally.

last_week_digest.title: New Kimsuky campaign compromised South Korean software vendors
last_week_digest.tldr: North Korean hackers from the Kimsuky group compromised South Korean software vendors, stealing customer data to facilitate downstream attacks. This supply chain breach highlights critical vulnerabilities in vendor security, signalling that global organisations must prioritise rigorous authentication and third-party risk management to prevent widespread infiltration.

last_week_digest.title: Suno, Paidwork Data Breaches Affect Tens of Millions of Accounts
last_week_digest.tldr: Massive data breaches at Suno and Paidwork have exposed the personal details, passwords, and financial information of tens of millions of global users. This incident underscores the persistent vulnerability of digital platforms, signalling an urgent requirement for enhanced authentication protocols to protect sensitive consumer data.

last_week_digest.title: Check Point warns of SmartConsole zero-day exploited in attacks
last_week_digest.tldr: Check Point has addressed an actively exploited zero-day vulnerability in its SmartConsole GUI, allowing unauthenticated attackers to gain administrator privileges. While affecting a small customer base, the flaw highlights the persistent risk of management interface exposure and the critical necessity for rapid patch deployment.

last_week_digest.title: South Korea discloses data breach impacting diplomats worldwide
last_week_digest.tldr: South Korea’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs confirmed a ten-month breach of its education platform, exposing the personal data of at least 6,000 diplomats. This incident highlights critical vulnerabilities in legacy systems, signalling that neglected infrastructure remains a significant target for sophisticated state-sponsored espionage operations.

last_week_digest.title: Russian hackers exploit Zimbra zero-click flaw for email theft
last_week_digest.tldr: Russian state-sponsored group Laundry Bear is exploiting a critical Zimbra zero-click vulnerability to exfiltrate ninety days of sensitive email data from government, defence, and energy sectors globally. By bypassing multi-factor authentication, attackers maintain persistent access, signalling an urgent industry shift towards prioritising rapid patch management and phishing-resistant authentication to defend against sophisticated, stealthy espionage campaigns.

last_week_digest.title: Clop ransomware targets Windchill, FlexPLM in data theft attacks
last_week_digest.tldr: The Clop ransomware gang is exploiting a critical vulnerability in PTC Windchill and FlexPLM software, enabling remote code execution and sensitive product data exfiltration. This campaign threatens over 30,000 global customers, including major aerospace and manufacturing firms. It signals a shift towards weaponising enterprise lifecycle management platforms, forcing urgent international regulatory intervention and patching.

last_week_digest.title: Ransomware gangs go after EMEA healthcare’s supply chain
last_week_digest.tldr: Ransomware gangs are increasingly targeting the EMEA healthcare supply chain, with 14 groups exploiting fragmented IT systems to disrupt critical services. These attacks, which caused 289 incidents in the EU during 2024, signal that operational downtime, rather than ransom payments, now drives billions in losses, threatening regional stability and patient safety across interconnected medical networks.

last_week_digest.title: Data Breach Confirmed After Australian Energy Giant Origin Is Hacked
last_week_digest.tldr: Australian energy giant Origin has confirmed a significant data breach after a threat actor claimed to have exfiltrated the personal information of two million customers. This incident threatens severe reputational damage and regulatory scrutiny, signalling a growing trend where critical infrastructure providers face heightened risks from sophisticated cybercriminals targeting vast repositories of sensitive consumer data globally.

last_week_digest.title: International alert spotlights Russia-linked attacks on Zimbra webmail
last_week_digest.tldr: Russian state-aligned group Laundry Bear is exploiting a Zimbra webmail vulnerability to conduct espionage against global government, defence, and financial sectors. By deploying zero-click payloads to exfiltrate sensitive communications, these attackers signal a shift toward sophisticated, persistent targeting. This campaign highlights the critical necessity for organisations to prioritise rapid patching to mitigate nation-state threats.

last_week_digest.title: ShinyHunters data leaks fuel $2,000 sextortion email scam
last_week_digest.tldr: Threat actors are leveraging data leaked by the ShinyHunters group from major firms like Amtrak and Panera Bread to launch widespread $2,000 sextortion scams. By weaponising exposed email addresses, attackers fabricate claims of device compromise to coerce victims. This trend signals that historical data breaches create long-term, compounding risks for global organisations and individuals.

last_week_digest.title: Australian energy provider Origin Energy disclosed a data breach impacting customer data
last_week_digest.tldr: Australian energy provider Origin Energy confirmed a data breach involving unauthorized access to customer records, with an attacker claiming to have stolen data from two million individuals. This incident, exposing names and partial financial details, highlights the growing vulnerability of critical infrastructure providers and underscores the urgent necessity for robust data protection across the global utilities sector.

last_week_digest.title: UAC-0099 Is Now Hiding Malware Inside a Fake Notepad++ Plugin to Target Ukrainian Organizations
last_week_digest.tldr: The Russia-aligned threat actor UAC-0099 is targeting Ukrainian organisations using a sophisticated phishing campaign that delivers malware via a trojanised Notepad++ plugin. By embedding malicious DLLs within legitimate software, attackers maintain persistent access to sensitive systems. This evolution signals a growing trend of adversaries weaponising trusted productivity tools to bypass traditional security defences.

last_week_digest.title: In Other News: Dolphin X AI-Powered Malware, Car Anti-Theft Device Hack, 400 Linux Kernel Flaws
last_week_digest.tldr: Recent security disclosures reveal critical vulnerabilities in Siemens industrial switches and a targeted espionage campaign against Zimbra webmail users, alongside a significant ransomware extortion attempt against Stadler Rail. These incidents highlight the escalating risks to global critical infrastructure and corporate data, signalling that sophisticated threat actors are increasingly exploiting diverse industrial and enterprise software ecosystems.

last_week_digest.title: 'Wrench' attacks against crypto holders appear to be on the rise
last_week_digest.tldr: Physical "wrench" attacks against cryptocurrency holders surged globally, with 52 incidents recorded in early 2026, marking a 33 percent year-on-year increase. These violent coercions resulted in reported losses reaching $124 million. This trend signals a dangerous shift where criminals bypass digital security by targeting individuals directly, highlighting critical vulnerabilities inherent in self-custody and personal operational security.

last_week_digest.title: DentaQuest disclosed a data breach that impacted +23 million individuals
last_week_digest.tldr: DentaQuest confirmed a significant data breach involving the theft of 234 gigabytes of sensitive health and personal information belonging to over 23 million individuals. This major incident highlights the persistent vulnerability of healthcare administrators to extortion groups and the critical necessity for robust data protection.

last_week_digest.title: Ernst & Young data breach claimed by ShinyHunters extortion gang
last_week_digest.tldr: The ShinyHunters extortion gang has claimed responsibility for breaching Ernst & Young via a supply-chain attack, potentially exposing sensitive client tax filings. This incident highlights the critical business risks posed by third-party service providers, signalling an urgent need for enhanced vendor security oversight globally.

last_week_digest.title: SourTrade Malvertising Campaign Secretly Builds Malware in the Browser
last_week_digest.tldr: The SourTrade malvertising campaign, active since 2024, now stealthily constructs malware within victims' browsers to bypass traditional network security. By assembling malicious payloads locally, attackers evade file fingerprinting, signalling a shift toward sophisticated, memory-based threats that undermine standard enterprise detection and defence capabilities globally.

last_week_digest.title: Coca-Cola Confirms Data Breach After Fairlife Ransomware Attack
last_week_digest.tldr: Coca-Cola confirmed a significant data breach following a ransomware attack on its Fairlife subsidiary by the Anubis cybercrime group. This incident, involving threats to leak sensitive information, highlights the escalating risk of supply chain vulnerabilities and the persistent operational threat posed by global ransomware syndicates.

last_week_digest.title: Hackers used autonomous AI agent to spy on Thailand's finance ministry
last_week_digest.tldr: Hackers deployed an autonomous AI agent to infiltrate Thailand’s Ministry of Finance, compromising internal systems and stealing credentials. This incident highlights a dangerous shift toward AI-driven espionage, signalling that automated, human-independent attack vectors now pose a critical, scalable threat to global government and corporate infrastructure.

last_week_digest.title: Coca-Cola Reveals Subsidiary Fairlife Suffered Data Breach
last_week_digest.tldr: Coca-Cola subsidiary Fairlife suffered a ransomware attack by the Anubis group, resulting in production outages and the theft of 671GB of internal data. This incident highlights how sensitive corporate information, beyond customer records, remains a critical vulnerability, signalling that organisations must urgently improve data segmentation to prevent widespread operational exposure.

last_week_digest.title: New Crypter-as-a-Service Cruciferra Fuels Stealthy Malware Attacks Worldwide
last_week_digest.tldr: The emergence of the Cruciferra crypter-as-a-service, priced up to $2,000 monthly, enables diverse criminal groups to bypass antivirus defences globally. By facilitating stealthy malware deployment across multiple sectors, this sophisticated, shared infrastructure signals a professionalised shift in cybercrime, complicating forensic investigations and undermining traditional signature-based security for businesses worldwide.

last_week_digest.title: Phishing Dominates as Initial Entry Method for Cyber-Attacks, as Hackers Hone Evasion Techniques
last_week_digest.tldr: Phishing accounted for over half of all cyber incidents investigated by Cisco Talos between March and June 2026, marking a significant quarterly increase. By weaponising trusted cloud platforms and QR codes to bypass security gateways, attackers are compromising credentials, signalling a critical need for organisations to adopt phishing-resistant authentication measures globally.

last_week_digest.title: Cyera Acquiring Oasis Security in $1 Billion Deal
last_week_digest.tldr: Cyera has acquired Oasis Security for $1 billion, integrating its agentic access management platform following Oasis’s recent $120 million Series B funding round. This significant consolidation signals a maturing cybersecurity market, where businesses are increasingly prioritising automated identity governance to mitigate complex operational risks across global, cloud-native digital infrastructure environments.

last_week_digest.title: India’s Bank of Baroda confirms cyber incident after hackers claim data theft
last_week_digest.tldr: Bank of Baroda confirmed a security breach after an employee’s email account was compromised, potentially exposing sensitive corporate and customer data. While core systems remained secure, the incident highlights the rising vulnerability of major Asian financial institutions to targeted data theft, signalling an urgent need for enhanced third-party and internal monitoring.

last_week_digest.title: Russian hackers exploit Exchange OWA zero-day for long-term mailbox access
last_week_digest.tldr: Russian state-sponsored group Laundry Bear is exploiting an Outlook Web Access zero-day to deploy OWAReaper, a sophisticated backdoor. Targeting global government and corporate sectors, the malware enables long-term mailbox persistence, signalling an alarming evolution in half-click exploits that bypass traditional credential rotation and system restoration.

last_week_digest.title: VPN Breach Exposes 58 Million Connection Logs Despite “No-Logs” Claims
last_week_digest.tldr: A breach of SplitVPN exposed 58 million connection logs and 23.4 million user records, contradicting its no-logs policy. This incident highlights the significant risks of centralised privacy services, as leaked metadata now potentially exposes users in restrictive regimes to severe real-world safety consequences.

last_week_digest.title: The Average Cost of a Data Breach Rises to $5 Million
last_week_digest.tldr: The global average cost of a data breach has climbed 12% to a record $4.99 million, impacting 602 organisations. This surge signals a shift toward multilayered extortion strategies, as AI-driven attacks increasingly target brand reputation and customer trust, forcing businesses to prioritise autonomous defences.

last_week_digest.title: Laundry Bear’s webmail hackers had more in store after February, report says
last_week_digest.tldr: Russian state-linked group Laundry Bear is targeting global government, telecommunications, and financial sectors using sophisticated OWAReaper malware. By exploiting Microsoft Outlook vulnerabilities via half-click attacks, these actors compromise credentials, signalling an alarming evolution in tradecraft that threatens persistent access across critical international infrastructure.

last_week_digest.title: ThreatLocker Raises $190 Million in Series F Funding
last_week_digest.tldr: Endpoint security provider ThreatLocker has secured $190 million in Series F funding, significantly increasing its previous $1.6 billion valuation. This substantial capital injection signals strong investor confidence in zero-trust architecture, reflecting a broader industry shift towards prioritising proactive application control to mitigate evolving global threats.

last_week_digest.title: North Korean hackers behind major open-source supply chain attacks, Amazon says
last_week_digest.tldr: North Korean threat actor SapphireSleet compromised four major JavaScript packages, including the widely used axios library, which sees 100 million weekly downloads. By socially engineering maintainers to distribute malicious updates, attackers infiltrated countless enterprise environments. This trend signals a shift toward targeting open-source supply chains to bypass individual security perimeters and facilitate global cyber theft.

last_week_digest.title: Horizon3.ai expands NodeZero with automated web application attack path testing
last_week_digest.tldr: Horizon3.ai has launched autonomous web application pentesting within its NodeZero platform to combat vulnerabilities arising from rapid generative AI deployments. By chaining exploits across infrastructure, cloud, and identity, the tool quantifies actual business risks. This shift signals an industry move away from noisy, theoretical scanning toward evidence-based security prioritisation against sophisticated, AI-driven adversary tactics.

last_week_digest.title: After the Break-In: What Attackers Do Once They're Already Inside
last_week_digest.tldr: Attackers exploiting a SQL injection vulnerability in a June incident demonstrated how threat actors dwell within networks to establish persistent backdoors, disable security controls, and deploy BadIIS malware for traffic manipulation. This shift from immediate data theft to long-term environmental compromise signals that businesses must prioritise post-breach detection and rigorous internal monitoring over perimeter-focused defences.

last_week_digest.title: Cisco warns of FMC static credential flaw exploited in zero-day attacks
last_week_digest.tldr: Cisco has confirmed active zero-day exploitation of a high-severity static credential vulnerability in its Secure Firewall Management Center software. This flaw allows unauthenticated remote access, potentially leading to privilege escalation. The incident highlights critical risks within enterprise network infrastructure, forcing organisations to urgently apply hot fixes to prevent unauthorised data exposure and compromise.

last_week_digest.title: CareCloud Data Breach Impacts Over 350,000
last_week_digest.tldr: CareCloud recently suffered a significant data breach involving its AWS environment, exposing the sensitive personal, financial, and medical information of over 350,000 individuals. This incident disrupts operational trust and highlights the critical vulnerability of cloud-hosted healthcare data, signalling an urgent industry-wide need for more robust security protocols to protect patient privacy against sophisticated attackers.
